purpose: Advance from known-city undated extents to a genuinely dated, spatially interpretable regional benchmark around AD200. Do not add warehouse mechanisms or tune the hierarchy to compensate for missing evidence.
priority: Resolve observation definition and support before fitting: independently documented survey footprint, site inclusion/detection limits, settlement type, occupation phase around AD200, and dated area or population evidence with explicit estimation method.
selection: Inspect metadata and methods for at most three period-appropriate regional survey/census sources, selected for coverage/date/method rather than model outcomes. Prefer directly archived scholarly Roman material spanning AD100–300. Do not claim an excavated-site catalogue is a complete survey, a household sample is a provincial census, or city occupation dates date its measured extent.
eligible_comparisons: With a justified footprint/observation model, declare simple spatial intensity or fixed-budget population baselines against the current recipe on identical support. If only a different observation is available, match the claim and scale explicitly. Reserve genuinely unused suitable observations for a final test only after exact cohort/metrics are declared.
stopping_rule: Record failures of date, footprint, population definition or observation completeness. If no source passes, present the gap and the most defensible bounded benchmark; do not manufacture population from area-density assumptions or silently open a reserved pool.
existing_size_result: The frozen hierarchy has modest added conditional area skill over M0, retains Egypt underprediction and aggregate area bias. These findings justify checking real regional observations, not a new H/capital parameter search.
deliverable: A concise source/case eligibility table and one declared regional observation contract. Then, only if support qualifies, a same-support regional baseline comparison. No claim of new blind evidence without exposure audit.
exclusions: No modern truck evidence, handling-rate search, new hierarchy tuning, food/work/climate/route solver, atlas change or automatic opening of reserved Buringh size/climate pools or the site-survey workbook.
